supplemental chromium (20 ppm in diet) increased weight gain of poults fed 23% protein, increased liver glycogen and active glycogen synthase, increased the in vitro incorporation of (C14)-glucose into glycogen, and had little effect on blood glucose or active phosphorylase.
supplemental chromium increased weight gain, liver glycogen and glycogen synthesis, while excess nicotinic acid decreased weight gain, liver phosphorylase and glycogen synthesis.
supplemental chromium increased liver glycogenic enzymes and in vitro glucose incorporation into glycogen during the basal, starvation and refed periods.

the effects of supplemental dietary chromium (20 ppm), nicotinic acid (250 ppm), and starvation-refeeding periods on growth, carbohydrate metabolism, and enzyme levels in the liver and skeletal muscles of turkey poults.
the effects of chromium and nicotinic acid supplementation on carbohydrate metabolism during the basal, starvation, or refeeding periods in turkey poults.
the effect of supplemental chromium and nicotinic acid in the diet of turkey poults.

supplemental chromium increases carbohydrate synthesis and storage during a starvation-refeed period.
